newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ says April unemployed data wrong to show rise.
newsitem.headline: NZ says April unemployed data wrong to show rise.

text.p: New Zealand's Employment Ministry said on Wednesday a computer error had caused an overstatement of over 6,100 people in the April registered unemployed count, and that in fact the number on the roll had fallen between March and April rather than rising as reported.
"There were 151,737 people registered with NZES at the end of April 1997. This represents a drop of 974 from March to April this year," the ministry said in a statement.
"I understand from officials that a change to a computer programme caused the register to be overstated by 6,104 at the end of April," minister Peter McCardle said.

"The correct figures now show that registered unemployment actually fell slightly over the month, despite the end of some seasonal work and the arrival of newly work-tested beneficiaries onto the register," he added.

The New Zealand Employment Service (NZES) had corrected the mistake and the minister said, "I have made it very clear that I expect future figures to be an accurate total of the numbers registered as unemployed".
Corrected regional statistics for April would now be released alongside the May register data due on June 12, he added.
